messages:
alex: heads-up — thinking through automatic fallback policies for canary rollouts. we need model-variant fallback, regional failover, and capacity fallback. what signals should trigger auto-fallbacks and what should the console API look like? :thinking:

maria: +1. important to define "guard rails". i'd start with signals: error-rate (>X% over Ys windows), p95 latency (>T ms), and queue depth / available capacity. also a soft signal for quality regressions (eval set mismatch) if available.

raj: agree on signals. question: who pays for the fallback when we shift traffic to a more expensive variant/region? need cost-awareness baked into policies (max-cost-multiplier or budget cap).

alex: good point. propose policy fields: `signals`, `conditions`, `fallback_chain` and `budget`. fallback_chain = ordered list e.g. [model-quant-8bit, model-16bit, regional-standby, degrade-to-embedding-only].

maria: rough config sketch (console + API schema):
```json
{
  "policy_name": "canary-autofallback-v1",
  "signals": { "error_rate": { "threshold_pct": 2.5, "window_sec": 120 }, "p95": { "threshold_ms": 1000, "window_sec": 60 } },
  "fallback_chain": [
    { "type": "model_variant", "id": "m-xl-8q", "max_cost_multiplier": 1.2 },
    { "type": "region", "id": "eu-west-standby", "max_failover_pct": 100 },
    { "type": "capacity_tier", "id": "burst-dedicated" }
  ],
  "cooldown_sec": 300,
  "consecutive_windows": 2
}
```

sophia: console UX thoughts: show live traffic split slider and a compact "fallback chain" pill that expands into the ordered list. expose an "execute fallback now" button for ops and a preview of predicted cost + latency impact. also surface telemetry (error rate, p95) inline next to the canary slider. :eyes:

opsbot: alert — canary id=canary-20250708 exceeded error_rate 3.4% over 120s at 1746860400.

canary-bot: automated suggestion: recommend fallback to model_variant m-xl-8q (8-bit) or region eu-west-standby. predicted latency impact -5% and cost +12%. to auto-apply run: `POST /api/rollouts/{id}/apply-fallback?choice=first`

alex: opsbot/canary-bot examples are helpful. need to formalize: fallback only after N consecutive windows and only if fallback reduces error_rate in simulation. also require an owner ack for cross-region failover by default (safety).

maria: implementation note — telemetry aggregation must be per-route, per-token-class (prompt vs completion), and tag with model-variant so we can compute deltas. prefer doing evaluation on a mirror stream + small shadow traffic to verify fallback efficacy before switching live.

raj: for Dedicated customers, fallback to other capacity tiers may violate contracts. we need policy scope: `scope: hosted|dedicated|private` and validate before auto-apply. if scope forbids fallback, only notify ops.

alex: good call. we also need API primitives: `POST /rollouts/{id}/policy` to set these policies, `GET /rollouts/{id}/policy/simulate?window=60` to run a simulation, and `POST /rollouts/{id}/policy/force-fallback` for manual ops.

sophia: UX: add small indicator if policy is "simulation-only" or "auto-apply-allowed". default should be simulation-only for new policies.

maria: on cooldowns — enforce jittered exponential backoff between fallback attempts, and include a manual rollback button that can revert fallback chain in one click.

alex: ok next steps: maria to draft API schema + simulation endpoint; sophia to mock console UI; raj to add contract checks for Dedicated/Private; i'll prototype a canary-bot rule that evaluates mirror stream and posts recommendations. who wants to own docs? :robot_face:

maria: i'll start the API doc. will post PR by EOD tomorrow.

raj: i'll check the contract edge-cases and list forbidden auto-fallbacks for Dedicated by EOD too.

sophia: mockups by Friday.

alex: thanks all — let's sync in the rollout sync on Thursday if needed. :thumbsup:
